text: If you do the hard path and it doesn't work, actually you still win because you've now done something hard. You've probably worked with smart people. You've learned something along the way that is valuable. I meet lots of job seekers.
speaker: Farhan Thawar
context: Lenny asks Farhan to explain his philosophy of choosing the harder path when deciding between options. Farhan explains that when you take the easy route and it fails, you learn nothing, but when you take the hard path and it fails, you still gain valuable skills and experience. He uses job searching as an example - instead of just sending out resumes, candidates should build something with a company's APIs to demonstrate skills and learn in the process.
text_ko: 힘든 길을 택해서 잘 안돼도, 사실 이긴 셈이에요. 힘든 일을 해봤다는 경험 자체가 남고, 아마 유능한 사람들과 함께 일해봤을 거고, 그 과정에서 값진 걸 배웠을 거예요. 저는 구직자(job seekers)들을 많이 만나요.
text_zh: 如果你选择了难走的路，就算最后没成功，其实你还是赚到了，因为你已经做过难事了。你很可能跟聪明人一起共事过，路上肯定学到了有价值的东西。我见过很多找工作的人。
text_es: Si tomas el camino difícil y no funciona, en realidad igual ganas porque ya hiciste algo complicado. Seguramente trabajaste con gente inteligente. Aprendiste algo en el proceso que tiene valor. Conozco a muchos candidatos.
key_sentence: You win by taking the hard path and learning valuable lessons along the way.
original_text: If you do the hard path and it doesn't work, actually you still win because you've now done something hard. You've probably worked with smart people. You've learned something along the way that is valuable. I meet lots of job seekers. I go, what are you doing to try to find a job? Are you really learning anything from sending out 10 resumes a day? Why don't you look at the API Docs and build something? Even if you don't get a job at Shopify, you've learned something.

vocabulary.definition: Having worth or significance; capable of providing useful benefits or advantages.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, 'valuable' often refers to assets, skills, or experiences that contribute positively to a company's success or competitive edge.
vocabulary.nuance: While 'valuable' generally implies high worth, it can also suggest subjective importance depending on context, such as personal or organizational priorities.

vocabulary.definition: Individuals who actively search for something, such as knowledge, employment, or opportunities.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the job market, 'seekers' typically refers to job seekers who are looking for employment opportunities and may engage in networking or skill development.
vocabulary.nuance: The term often conveys a sense of proactivity and determination, distinguishing them from passive candidates.

vocabulary.definition: Acquired knowledge or skills through experience or education; possessing deep understanding in a particular area.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a business context, 'learned' can describe individuals who have gained expertise through practical experience, training, or continuous professional development.
vocabulary.nuance: While 'learned' can imply formal education, it often emphasizes practical knowledge gained through real-world application.

text: I have been in many situations with many sharp people who have said to me, that's the stupidest fucking question I've ever heard. My goal there is not to annoy the person, but it's to understand the content.
speaker: Farhan Thawar
context: Lenny asks about Farhan's quote that looking stupid in public is his superpower. Farhan explains that he's comfortable asking questions that others might consider dumb because his priority is understanding the content rather than protecting his image. He shares that even successful business people have harshly criticized his questions, but he persists because learning is more important than appearing smart.
text_ko: 저는 여러 상황에서 예리한 분들이 저에게 “이건 내가 들어본 것 중에 가장 어처구니없는 질문이야”라고 말하는 걸 많이 겪었어요. 제 목표는 그 사람을 짜증나게 하려는 게 아니라, 내용을 제대로 이해하려는 거예요.
text_zh: 我遇到过很多聪明人，他们会对我说，这是我听过的最蠢的问题了。但我的目的不是要惹他们生气，而是想真正搞懂这个事儿。
text_es: He estado en muchas situaciones con gente muy lista que me ha dicho: "esa es la pregunta más estúpida que he escuchado en mi puta vida". Mi objetivo ahí no es joder a la persona, sino entender realmente el contenido.
key_sentence: Sharp people often dismiss questions, but understanding content is the goal.

vocabulary.definition: To understand means to grasp the meaning, significance, or nature of something, often involving comprehension of complex ideas.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a business context, understanding customer needs or market trends is crucial for effective strategy formulation and decision-making.
vocabulary.nuance: Understanding can imply a deeper level of insight beyond mere knowledge; use it when emphasizing comprehension of complexities.

vocabulary.definition: Sharp refers to someone who is quick-witted, intelligent, and able to think critically or analytically.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the business world, sharp individuals are often valued for their ability to solve problems creatively and make strategic decisions under pressure.
vocabulary.nuance: While 'sharp' generally has a positive connotation, it can also imply a certain level of aggressiveness or intensity; use it carefully in professional settings.

vocabulary.definition: Content refers to the information, material, or subject matter contained within a document, presentation, or communication.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business and marketing, creating valuable content is essential for engaging customers and enhancing brand visibility across various platforms.
vocabulary.nuance: While 'content' can refer to any type of material, in digital marketing, it often implies a focus on quality and relevance; avoid using it in contexts where specificity is required.

text: They're mostly different people, but they're similar in one thing is that they haven't... they have an irrational view of what the world should look like over the next decade or so.
speaker: Farhan Thawar
context: Lenny points out that Farhan has worked for a different billionaire each decade of his career and asks what connects these successful leaders. Farhan explains that while these leaders are different people, they share the ability to envision how the world will look decades in the future. He recognizes that his strength is execution - moving toward their vision incrementally - rather than having the visionary ability himself.
text_ko: 대부분은 서로 다른 사람들이에요. 다만 한 가지는 비슷해요 — 바로 앞으로 10년쯤 세상이 어떻게 돼야 한다고 비합리적으로 생각한다는 점이에요.
text_zh: 这些人大部分都不一样，但有一个共同点，就是他们对未来十年左右世界应该是什么样子，想法都不太现实。
text_es: Son personas muy diferentes en su mayoría, pero tienen algo en común: no tienen... digamos que tienen una visión poco realista de cómo debería verse el mundo en los próximos diez años.
key_sentence: they have an irrational view of what the world should look like over the next decade or so.
original_text: They're mostly different people, but they're similar in one thing is that they haven't... they have an irrational view of what the world should look like over the next decade or so. They're very long-term thinkers, very rational in that they'll look and say, 'Hey, in 10, 15, 20, 25 years, this is what the world's going to look like.' And I'm not good at seeing that vision, but I'm good at trying to move towards that vision 1% a week.

vocabulary.definition: Not based on reason or logic; exhibiting a lack of sound judgment.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, an irrational decision may stem from emotional responses rather than analytical thinking, potentially leading to poor strategic choices.
vocabulary.nuance: While 'irrational' often carries a negative connotation, it can also describe unconventional thinking that may lead to innovative solutions.

vocabulary.definition: A period of ten years, often used as a unit of time to assess trends or changes.
vocabulary.businessContext: Businesses often analyze performance and market trends over a decade to understand long-term growth patterns and strategic shifts.
vocabulary.nuance: The term 'decade' can imply a significant timeframe for evaluating progress, making it suitable for discussions about long-term planning.

vocabulary.definition: Having characteristics in common; resembling each other in some aspects.
vocabulary.businessContext: In market analysis, identifying similar products or services can help businesses understand competitive landscapes and customer preferences.
vocabulary.nuance: The term 'similar' can suggest a degree of comparison that may not imply exact equivalence, making it useful in nuanced discussions of differentiation.

text: It is the most underutilized management tool in engineering, bar none. It is just not used as much as it could be. So pair programming, for those who don't know, it's two people on one computer. The throughput limiter is not hands-on keyboard.
speaker: Farhan Thawar
context: Lenny asks why Farhan is such a big advocate for pair programming, since it seems counterintuitive to have two engineers working on one computer. Farhan argues that pair programming is incredibly underused in engineering management. He explains that the bottleneck in software development isn't typing speed but finding the right solution to problems - and two people working together are much better at this than one person alone.
text_ko: 페어 프로그래밍(pair programming)은 엔지니어링에서 관리 도구로는 단연 가장 덜 활용되는 수단이에요. 실제로는 더 많이 쓸 수 있는데 그렇게 안 쓰이는 경우가 많아요. 페어 프로그래밍이 뭔지 모르는 분들을 위해 말하면, 두 명이 한 대의 컴퓨터에서 같이 작업하는 방식이에요. 처리량을 제한하는 요인(throughput limiter)은 키보드를 직접 두드리는 사람(hands-on keyboard)이 아니에요.
text_zh: 这绝对是工程管理中最被低估的工具，没有之一。大家根本没有充分利用起来。结对编程(pair programming)，不了解的朋友，就是两个人用一台电脑写代码。瓶颈其实不在于谁来敲键盘。
text_es: Es la herramienta de gestión más desperdiciada en ingeniería, sin duda alguna. Simplemente no se usa ni la mitad de lo que debería. Entonces, la programación en pareja (pair programming), para los que no la conocen, son dos personas trabajando en una sola computadora. Lo que limita la productividad no es quién tiene las manos en el teclado.
key_sentence: Pair programming is the most underutilized management tool in engineering, bar none.
original_text: It is the most underutilized management tool in engineering, bar none. It is just not used as much as it could be. So pair programming, for those who don't know, it's two people on one computer. The throughput limiter is not hands-on keyboard. The limiter is where is the good elegant solution? How do we think through the problem and build the right solution for the problem at hand?

vocabulary.definition: Not used to its full potential or capacity; insufficiently employed.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business and technology, 'underutilized' often refers to resources, tools, or strategies that are available but not being maximized for efficiency or effectiveness.
vocabulary.nuance: The term carries a connotation of missed opportunities and inefficiency, often implying that improvement is possible.

vocabulary.definition: The amount of material or items passing through a system or process, often measured over a specific period.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a business or tech context, throughput is critical for evaluating the efficiency of processes, such as production lines or data processing systems.
vocabulary.nuance: While often associated with speed, throughput also emphasizes the capacity and effectiveness of a system to handle tasks or data.

text: Everyone says, 'Oh yeah, work hard and do more hours when you're young, whatever.' I'm like, 'What if you just did more per minute?' Like quickly get through things.
speaker: Farhan Thawar
context: Lenny asks about creating intensity in organizations, specifically Farhan's philosophy of expending more energy per hour rather than working longer hours. Farhan challenges the conventional wisdom of working more hours when young, suggesting instead that people should focus on accomplishing more within the same timeframe. He points out that highly skilled people can produce quality work faster, not just work longer.
text_ko: 다들 '젊을 때는 더 열심히 일하고 근무 시간을 늘려라'고들 하죠. 저는 '그렇다면 시간 자체를 늘리기보다 같은 시간에 분당 더 많은 성과를 내면 어떨까요?' 즉, 일을 빠르게 처리하자는 거예요.
text_zh: 大家都说"趁年轻多加班多熬夜什么的"，我就想，为什么不提高效率呢？快速把事情搞定不是更好吗？
text_es: Todo el mundo dice, 'Sí, claro, trabaja duro y echa más horas cuando eres joven, lo típico.' Pero yo pienso, '¿Y si simplemente rindieras más por minuto?' O sea, hacer las cosas rápido y ya.
key_sentence: What if you just did more per minute?
original_text: Everyone says, 'Oh yeah, work hard and do more hours when you're young, whatever.' I'm like, 'What if you just did more per minute?' Like quickly get through things. I think there's another unintuitive fact is that people who are really good can actually output high-quality collateral quickly.

text: We can always almost find a million-plus lines of code to delete, which is insane. But at the same time, I applaud the teams for going after the cruft and the code base. And everything gets easier, right? Code loads faster. It's easier to understand.
speaker: Farhan Thawar
context: Lenny asks about Shopify's initiative to delete code and simplify their codebase. Farhan explains that they have a Delete Code Club and regularly find millions of lines of code that can be removed during hack days. He sees this as beneficial because removing unnecessary code makes everything faster and easier to understand, though he acknowledges it might seem counterintuitive to celebrate deleting work.
text_ko: 우리는 거의 항상 백만 줄이 넘는 코드를 지워도 될 부분을 찾아낼 수 있어요. 정말 말도 안 돼요. 하지만 동시에 그런 쓸데없는 코드(cruft)와 코드베이스(code base)를 정리하러 나선 팀들은 정말 칭찬받아 마땅해요. 그러면 모든 게 더 쉬워져요. 코드 로딩도 빨라지고 이해하기도 쉬워져요.
text_zh: 我们几乎总能找到上百万行可以删掉的代码，这简直太疯狂了。不过同时我也得给团队点个赞，他们敢于清理那些冗余代码和代码库。然后你知道吗，一切都变得更容易了，对吧？代码跑得更快，也更好理解了。
text_es: Siempre podemos encontrar más de un millón de líneas de código para eliminar, lo cual es una locura. Pero a la vez, aplaudo a los equipos por ir tras toda esa basura (cruft) y limpiar la base de código. Y todo se vuelve más fácil, ¿no? El código carga más rápido. Es más fácil de entender.
key_sentence: Teams are going after the cruft, making the code base easier to understand.

vocabulary.definition: To express approval or admiration for someone’s actions or achievements, often through clapping or verbal praise.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a corporate setting, applauding team efforts can foster a positive culture, encourage collaboration, and motivate employees to strive for excellence.
vocabulary.nuance: The term 'applaud' conveys a strong sense of appreciation, but it may not be appropriate in situations requiring constructive criticism.
